accuracy.evidence: Facts checked: ladybirds, like all insects, have 6 legs; spiders have 8; garden snails move on a single muscular foot and have two pairs of tentacles; earthworms have no eyes; bees have two pairs of wings, black stripes and antennae.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips in early observational drawing: drawing a remembered symbol or cartoon, adding faces, legs and smiles, guessing numbers and colours, and stopping after one quick look.

lab_distinct.evidence: flaglook puts a real specimen beside the child's drawing and compares them: counting legs, rubbing out made-up parts, colouring by looking back and a draggable magnifier; no other lab compares a record with its object.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step acts out one part of the look-draw-look-again loop: counted legs set the drawing, rub-outs only work on made-up parts, a wrong colour says look back, and the magnifier reveals parts to add.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions carry tempting wrong options the lab tests: 4 or 8 legs on a ladybird, legs on a snail, picking a favourite colour when unsure, and stopping once the drawing looks done.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six Challenge questions with twelve specific slip messages, e.g. '8 legs is a spider. A ladybird has 6 legs.' and 'A cartoon snail is made up. Look at a real one.'

accessibility.evidence: Canvas aria-label updates with every action, all controls are buttons with labels and aria-pressed for colours, white text only on dark swatches, and reduced motion speeds up Show me.

mobile.evidence: On an iPhone 13 the two panels sit side by side above 56 px buttons, every drag has a button twin, the magnifier drag is clamped to the real panel, and the lab passed the phone walkthrough.

no_filler.evidence: Every step is one or two short sentences tied to an action (count, rub out, colour, look closer, pick); no warm-up phrases, and the adult text goes straight to the EYFS goal and the common mistakes.

readability.evidence: Child text uses short sentences and words like look, draw, count, real and made up, for a 4 or 5 year old read aloud; numbers stay at 8 or below; the adult text names the EYFS Natural World goal and KS1 observing closely.
